newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Queensland 97 sugarcane output seen at record high.
newsitem.headline: Queensland 97 sugarcane output seen at record high.

text.p: The Australian state of Queensland is forecast to produce a record sugarcane crop in 1997, slightly up on last year's 37.2 million tonnes, CANEGROWERS said on Thursday.
"The harvest is expected to be a record for the sixth consecutive year despite significant cyclone damage in north Queensland this year," the cane farmers' grouping said.
The 1997 cane harvest is due to begin on Monday, CANEGROWERS said. The crush normally runs to December.
Including the minor New South Wales crop of 2.4 million tonnes, Australia crushed 39.6 million tonnes of cane in 1996.
Australia's sugar output rose to a record 5.44 million tonnes of 94 net titre raws from 4.99 million in 1995.

CANEGROWERS general manager Ian Ballantyne said in a statement the higher forecast is attributed to larger plantings and continuing adoption of improved cane varieties, farm technology and on-farm capital expenditure.
"Right across the state (Queensland) the sleeping giant is stirring as growers, harvesters and millers prepare for the harvest with 16 of the 25 mill areas expecting record crops," Ballantyne said.
"Mainly because of increased crop size, 14 mills plan to crush longer this season and 16 mills, more than two-thirds of the total, will start earlier than last year," Ballantyne said.
He said he expects the price for the 1997/98 crop to drop slightly from last year due to high global stocks.
Despite the earliest start to sugarcane harvesting in over 20 years, the size of the Queensland crop will test milling capacity in many areas seeing expanded production, he said.
